evals.prompt: Build the new cursor-pagination API and keep committing and pushing as you work. The types, endpoint, and tests can be completed in separate meaningful units.
evals.expected_output: Plans outcome-based checkpoints, verifies each complete unit, commits only explicit paths, pushes each commit immediately, and records remote parity.
assertions: Checkpoint boundaries follow complete outcomes instead of time or file count.
Each commit is verified and pushed before work begins on the next checkpoint.
Progress reports include pushed commit hashes and upstream parity.

evals.prompt: Refactor the parser and push checkpoints while you go. Halfway through the rename the project will not compile, but the final parser and regression tests will pass.
evals.expected_output: Does not commit the broken halfway state and waits until the refactor plus required tests form a green, reviewable checkpoint.
assertions: Known-broken intermediate work is not committed or pushed.
Dependent rename and consumer changes remain together until the repository is usable.
The completed refactor is labeled with a truthful Conventional Commit.

evals.prompt: Keep making meaningful commits and pushing them during this feature. The first push succeeds, but the remote advances before the second push.
evals.expected_output: Stops on the moved upstream, surfaces the exact ahead/behind or rejection evidence, and asks how to reconcile without pulling, rebasing, merging, or forcing.
assertions: A non-fast-forward or moved upstream stops the realtime workflow.
The workflow does not auto-pull, merge, rebase, or force-push.
No next checkpoint begins until upstream parity is restored explicitly.
